column1: # p405 -- the 52nd Moodle plugin grant, and the first that is NOT GPL-3.0-or-later.
# Read first-hand from a FULL clone of marcosnahuel/moodle-mcp at HEAD d5ca68e8cd1b (2026-05-03),
# 2026-10-23.  p401 measured 60 Moodle plugin slugs, read 51 grants and published "all 51 are
# GPL-3.0-or-later ... Not one MIT, Apache-2.0 or BSD in 51 reads".  This is a 52nd instance in a
# channel p401's two-channel ladder does not have: the plugin declares NOTHING and inherits the
# grant from a licence file ABOVE it in the tree.
# channel P = the grant in the header of the plugin's own PHP files (p401's channel P)
# channel L = a licence-shaped file inside the plugin directory  (p401's channel L)
# channel A = the nearest licence-shaped file in an ANCESTOR directory              <- NEW

column3: MIT at the repository root; npm @nahuelalbornoz/moodle-mcp; 10 tags v0.1.0..v0.5.1-plugin-v0.4.7; 65 commits, single author Nahuel <nahuelachu@gmail.com>
declared in plugin-companion/local_italiciamcp/version.php; a real Moodle local plugin -- db/services.php, db/access.php, lang/en/, 13 classes/external/ WS functions
Moodle 4.0 to 5.1 -- DECLARED, unlike p404's ADORSYS-GIS which dropped its $plugin->supported line
ZERO of 18 carry any GPL mention -- not the "version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version" paragraph, not the word GPL anywhere
no LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING or LICENCE at any path inside the plugin directory
repository root LICENSE, 1065 B, title line "MIT License"; README section reads "MIT (c) 2026 Italicia"
the only grant that reaches this Moodle plugin is the repository's MIT file, which sits two directories above it
the uniformity claim is now one counter-instance short, and the counter-instance is invisible to BOTH of p401's channels

a Moodle plugin calling Moodle's GPL APIs is normally held to GPL distribution terms, so an MIT-declared plugin is most likely a defect on the AUTHOR's side.  p401's boundary rule is UNCHANGED: a studio's permissive code still belongs outside the plugin boundary.  This row is a reason to ask the question in diligence, never a permissive Moodle plugin to build on
